documents.title: Mathematics, Class X, Secondary Curriculum Part 1, 2026-27
documents.extraction: pdftotext -layout (poppler 25.x), cross-checked against a python-standard-library extractor

objectives: Develops understanding of numbers, including the set of real numbers and its properties
Extends the understanding of powers (radical powers) and exponents
Applies Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic to solve problems related to real life contexts
contents: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic - statements after reviewing work done earlier and after illustrating and motivating through examples
Proofs of irrationality of √2, √3, √5
topics.name: Real numbers

objectives: Develops a relationship between algebraic and graphical methods of finding the zeroes of a polynomial
contents: Zeros of a polynomial
Relationship between zeros and coefficients of quadratic polynomials
topics.name: Polynomials

objectives: Describes plotting a pair of linear equations and graphically finding the solution
Models and solves contextualised problems using equations (e.g., simultaneous linear equations in two variables)
contents: Pair of linear equations in two variables and graphical method of their solution, consistency/inconsistency
Algebraic conditions for number of solutions
Solution of a pair of linear equations in two variables algebraically - by substitution, by elimination
topics.name: Pair of linear equations in two variables
topics.source_title: PAIR OF LINEAR EQUATIONS IN TWO VARIABLES

objectives: Demonstrates strategies of finding roots and determining the nature of roots of a quadratic equation
contents: Standard form of a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, (a ≠ 0)
Solutions of quadratic equations (only real roots) by factorization, and by using quadratic formula. Relationship between discriminant and nature of roots
Situational problems based on quadratic equations related to day-to-day activities to be incorporated
topics.name: Quadratic equations

objectives: Develops strategies to apply the concept of A.P. to daily life situations
contents: Motivation for studying Arithmetic Progression
Derivation of the nth term and sum of the first n terms of AP and their application in solving daily life problems
topics.name: Arithmetic progressions

objectives: Derives formulae to establish relations for geometrical shapes in the context of a coordinate plane, such as, finding the distance between two given points, to determine the coordinates of a point between any two given points
contents: Review: Concepts of coordinate geometry. Distance formula. Section formula (internal division)
topics.name: Coordinate Geometry

objectives: Works out ways to differentiate between congruent and similar figures
Establishes properties for similarity of two triangles logically using different geometric criteria established earlier such as, Basic Proportionality Theorem, etc
contents: Definitions, examples, counter examples of similar triangles
(Prove) If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio
State (without proof) If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, the line is parallel to the third side
State (without proof) If in two triangles, the corresponding angles are equal, their corresponding sides are proportional and the triangles are similar
State (without proof) If the corresponding sides of two triangles are proportional, their corresponding angles are equal and the two triangles are similar
State (without proof) If one angle of a triangle is equal to one angle of another triangle and the sides including these angles are proportional, the two triangles are similar
topics.name: Triangles

objectives: Derives proofs of theorems related to the tangents of circles
contents: Tangent to a circle at point of contact
(Prove) The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact
(Prove) The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal
topics.name: Circles

objectives: Understands the definitions of the basic trigonometric functions (including the introduction of the sine and cosine functions)
contents: Trigonometric ratios of an acute angle of a right-angled triangle. Proof of their existence (well defined)
Motivate the ratios whichever are defined at 0° and 90°. Values of the trigonometric ratios of 30°, 45° and 60°
Relationships between the ratios
topics.name: Introduction to trigonometry

objectives: Uses Trigonometric identities to solve problems
contents: Proof and applications of the identity sin² A + cos² A = 1
Only simple identities to be given
topics.name: Trigonometric identities

objectives: Applies Trigonometric ratios in solving problems in daily life contexts like finding heights of different structures or distance from them
contents: Simple problems on heights and distances. Problems should not involve more than two right triangles. Angles of elevation / depression should be only 30°, 45°, and 60°
topics.name: Heights and distances: Angle of elevation, Angle of Depression
topics.source_title: HEIGHTS AND DISTANCES: Angle of elevation, Angle of Depression

objectives: Derives and uses formulae to calculate areas of plane figures
contents: Area of sectors and segments of a circle

Problems based on areas and perimeter/circumference of the above said plane figures. (In calculating area of segment of a circle, problems should be restricted to central angle of 60°, 90° and 120° only)
topics.name: Areas related to circles

objectives: Visualises and uses mathematical thinking to discover formulae to calculate surface areas and volumes of solid objects (cubes, cuboids, spheres, hemispheres, right circular cylinders/cones, and their combinations)
contents: Surface areas and volumes of combinations of any two of the following: cubes, cuboids, spheres, hemispheres and right circular cylinders/cones
topics.name: Surface areas and volumes

objectives: Calculates mean, median and mode for different sets of data related with real life contexts
contents: Mean, median and mode of grouped data (bimodal situation to be avoided)
topics.name: Statistics

objectives: Applies concepts from probability to solve problems on the likelihood of everyday events
contents: Classical definition of probability
Simple problems on finding the probability of an event
topics.name: Probability

note: Units and marks are the course structure on page 2. Each topic's `contents` are the document's numbered content entries and its `objectives` are the document's own competencies column, verbatim. The document covers Mathematics Standard (041); the Basic (241) paper is the same syllabus with a different question paper design.
